([[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]) | college = [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]] (2022–2023) | highlights = * Second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2023) * AAC All-Freshman Team (2023) }} '''Taylor Hendricks''' (born November 22, 2003) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF Knights]] of the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC). As a freshman, he was a Second-team All-AAC and AAC All-Freshman Team selection. He was a three-time [[Florida High School Athletic Association]] (FHSSA) champion. ==Early life and high school career== Hendricks grew up in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]] and initially attended [[NSU University School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/draft-risers-inside-ucf-forward-taylor-hendricks-ascension-into-stardom|title=Draft Risers: Inside UCF Forward Taylor Hendricks' Ascension into Stardom|first=Nick|last=Crain|website=[[SI.com]]|date=December 20, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} The 2018–19 University team with, which included [[Vernon Carey Jr.]], [[Scottie Barnes]], Jace and [[Jett Howard]], successfully defended its [[FHSSA]] Class 5A State championship with a victory over [[Andrew Jackson High School (Jacksonville)|Andrew Jackson High School]], despite Carey being sidelined for the championship game.{{cite web|url=https://www.theledger.com/picture-gallery/news/local/2019/03/07/class-5a-final-university-72/66145967007/|title=Class 5A Final: University 72, Andrew Jackson 46|accessdate=February 4, 2023|date=March 16, 2019|work=[[The Ledger]]|author=}}{{cite web |last1=Lichtenstein |first1=Adam |title=University School — again with Carey sidelined — rolls to its second straight Class 5A state title |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-us-5a-sf-bhoops-20190307-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |accessdate=January 21, 2020 |date=March 7, 2019}} He transferred to [[Calvary Christian Academy (Florida)|Calvary Christian Academy]] after his sophomore year.{{cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-hs-boys-basketball-preview-2020-20201215-tezilaicpbb6nec4funiws7nqm-story.html|title=Boys basketball preview: Stacked Calvary Christian seeks national stage (plus other teams to watch)|work=[[Sun-Sentinel]]|date=December 15, 2020|access-date=January 12, 2023}} Hendricks averaged 14.1 points, 9.1 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks per game during his junior season while Calvary Christian won the Florida 3A state championship. As a senior, he was named the [[Broward County]] Player of the Year after averaging 15.1 points and 8.2 rebounds per game as Calvary Christian repeated as state champions.{{cite web|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/article257843053.html|title=Taylor Hendricks: Broward Boys' Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=April 15, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} Hendricks was rated a four-star recruit and committed to play [[college basketball]] at UCF over offers from the likes of Florida, Florida State, Miami, LSU, Memphis, and Iowa State.{{cite web|url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/taylor-hendricks-focused-on-his-season|title=Taylor Hendricks focused on his season|first=Jamie|last=Shaw|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=January 24, 2021|access-date=January 12, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/recruiting/fl-sp-hs-hendricks-ucf-20210320-uc3q7atarvetpedgb63eg7r744-story.html|title=Calvary Christian's Taylor and Tyler Hendricks commit to UCF|work=[[Sun-Sentinel]]|date=March 21, 2021|access-date=January 12, 2023}} His commitment made him the highest-ranked recruit in UCF history.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/ucf/ucf-basketball/ucf-knights-taylor-hendricks|title=UCF’s Taylor Hendricks is as Good as Advertised|first=Jack|last=Edwards|website=[[SI.com]]|date=December 13, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} ==College career== Hendricks entered his freshman season at UCF as the Knights' starting power forward.{{cite web|url=https://ucf.rivals.com/news/taylor-hendricks-excited-to-make-his-college-debut|title=Taylor Hendricks excited to make his college debut|first=Brandon|last=Helwig|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=November 2, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} On November 8, 2022, he opened the season with a 23-point, 2-steal and 3-block effort against [[2022–23 UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball team|UNC Asheville]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401488666|title=Pember's 40, Abee's 3s in 2OT get UNC Asheville past UCF|accessdate=February 13, 2023|date=November 8, 2022|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} He was named the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) Rookie of the Week for a conference record four consecutive weeks (November 21 through December 12).{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/ucf-knights/os-sp-ucf-knights-basketball-taylor-hendricks-aac-johnny-dawkins-20221213-aqrddargt5a6jlsadwwgcpz6jy-story.html|title=Taylor Hendricks makes 2023|date=December 12, 2022|publisher=[[American Athletic Conference]]}} The only other player to win the American Athletic Conference Rookie of the Week award three weeks in a row was [[Austin Nichols (basketball)|Austin Nichols]].{{cite web|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2022/12/5/mens-basketball-temples-battle-ucf-hendricks-earn-weekly-honors.aspx|title=Temple's Battle, UCF's Hendricks January 16, 2023, he tied [[Jalen Duren]], [[Precious Achiuwa]] and [[Dedric Lawson]] for the conference single-season record.{{cite web|url=https://ucfknights.com/news/2023/1/16/mens-basketball-hendricks-earns-sixth-aac-rookie-of-the-week-honor.aspx|title=Hendricks Earns Sixth AAC Rookie of the Week Honor: Freshman Taylor
